Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap delivers a smooth, judder-free experience that suits Metro Exodus's pacing well. FSR upscaling from 1024x640 recovers most visual sharpness while keeping the GPU within budget across both indoor and outdoor areas.

profiles.Summary: Metro Exodus runs on the Steam Deck via Proton with gold/trending-platinum compatibility, making it broadly playable, though its demanding PC requirements (recommended GTX 1070+) mean the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU needs low-to-medium settings and FSR upscaling to maintain comfortable frame rates. Expect 30–45 fps depending on the profile, with performance varying notably between open-world outdoor levels and tighter indoor sections.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU capability. On first run, check frame rate in an outdoor area (Volga or Caspian) — if it dips below 30 fps consistently, lower shadows and global illumination first, or move to the Max Battery profile.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and let Deck FSR upscale to 1280x800; the 8 W TDP and 900 MHz GPU clock keep thermals and fan noise low. Best for long travel sessions — the game remains readable and playable at these settings despite the visual compromise.

KnownIssues: The Enhanced Edition (DX12/ray-tracing) is not supported on the Steam Deck GPU; the standard DX11 version must be used.
Some players report stuttering during shader compilation on first launch; running through a few areas before judging performance is recommended.
Anti-cheat or launcher prompts may require brief touchscreen interaction on first boot.
Outdoor open-world levels (e.g. Volga, Caspian) are significantly more demanding than linear indoor chapters and may cause frame-rate dips even on lower settings.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Uncapping the TDP lets the APU boost freely for the best possible frame rates, but 60 fps is not reliably sustained in dense outdoor scenes — expect 40–55 fps with occasional dips. If consistent smoothness matters more than peak fps, drop back to the Optimal profile.

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and frame cap gives a smooth, judder-free experience that suits the game's cinematic pacing. Medium textures and shadows noticeably improve image quality over Low while FSR upscaling from 1024x640 keeps GPU load manageable.

profiles.Summary: Metro Exodus runs on the Steam Deck at playable frame rates using low settings and FSR upscaling, sitting right at the minimum PC spec class for the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU. The Enhanced Edition's ray-tracing features are not supported on Deck hardware, so the standard edition or disabling RT options is required.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs relative to the Deck's GTX 1050 Ti-class GPU. On first run, check frame rate in an open outdoor area — if it drops below 30 fps on Optimal, switch to Max Battery and reduce texture resolution to Low.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a 7 W TDP cap keeps the GPU well within limits for extended sessions. Disabling motion blur and depth of field recovers GPU headroom at minimal visual cost.

KnownIssues: The Enhanced Edition requires Nvidia RTX or AMD RX GPU for ray-tracing — these features are unavailable on the Steam Deck; use the standard edition.
Shader compilation stutters may occur on first launch or when entering new areas for the first time.
HDR output may not function correctly under Proton on the Steam Deck OLED.
A mouse cursor may appear in some menus; using full controller input works around this.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at medium settings pushes the Deck's GPU hard; frame rate will be unstable in dense outdoor areas and will not consistently reach 60 fps. Consider dropping to the Optimal profile if stutters are frequent in open-world sections.
